riders: Your Attack action gives three attacks at cultivation level 11 and four at level 17.
An extra attack granted by some other ability, outside the attacks of your Attack action, does not gain another extra attack unless that ability says it does.
Body Tempering does not resist physical damage created or empowered by cultivation abilities or magical powers, unless another feature says it does.
You can hold your breath for ten times as long as usual.
Caltrops, thorns, splinters and other small everyday hazards cannot hurt you, unless they are magical or part of an active attack or trap.

After damage is determined but before you lose Hit Points, you may spend up to your Proficiency Bonus in Stamina, your physical cultivation energy. Stamina Guard uses your Reaction and reduces that damage by 1d10 per point spent.
Roll all the Stamina Guard dice and add their results to find the reduction.
Apply Immunity, Resistance, Vulnerability and other modifiers before subtracting Stamina Guard's reduction. Lose Hit Points only for the damage remaining.
Stamina Guard reduces the damage as a whole, whatever mix of damage types it is. You choose which types it comes off first when that matters.

If Stamina Guard brings the damage to 0, anything that needed you to take damage does not happen. Something that needed only the attack to land still happens, as does a condition applied no matter what.
Stamina Guard cannot reduce the loss of maximum Hit Points or Cultivation Points, a cost you chose to pay, damage that says it cannot be reduced, or anything that is not damage.
The Second Defensive Discipline granted at CL15 is chosen under Cultivated Response.

At the start of your turn, before other recovery, if you have no Qi (your cultivation energy), regain Qi equal to your Proficiency Bonus, once per scene. This does not remove Exhaustion from running out of Qi.
Independent Concentration uses your Reaction and costs 1 Qi to add your Proficiency Bonus to a failed Constitution save to maintain a Qi-powered feature, once per round.
Independent Concentration’s bonus is not saving-throw proficiency.
Your Domain Armament lasts while you are Incapacitated, and ends if you become Unconscious.

Once per activation, when a Qi-powered feature deals damage, add your Qi Cultivation key ability modifier to one damage roll. Qi is your cultivation energy; an ordinary weapon attack does not qualify just because you cultivate Qi.

Qualifying features are Qi Cultivation Path and Subpath features, Qi-powered Sphere talents, Recorded Arts, Forged Techniques and Immortal Arts that use Qi, and weapon attacks that the text says deliver Qi-powered cultivation damage. A Barrage, volley, chain or any other multi-attack activation gets the bonus once for the whole activation, not once per attack.

Tempered Response does not stack with saving-throw proficiency from another source. If you already add your Proficiency Bonus to that saving throw, the person running the game must ensure it is not added again.
You gain a second Defensive Discipline through Indomitable Body at CL13. The table asks which saving throw your Discipline covers the first time it matters; a second Discipline is not asked for yet.

At CL15 you learn a second Defensive Discipline, and at CL20 all three. TABLE NOTE: Ask the player to choose which saving throw each Discipline covers during character build or level-up; this note does not add a combat trigger.
